look_here_first: TEXAS TRIDENS — look for a perennial tuft with a relatively short, loose, FLEXUOUS panicle; slender branches are often bare near their bases and carry hanging groups of multi-flowered spikelets toward their ends. Purpletop can also have bare branch bases and rosy spikelets. Under 10–20× confirm two thin glumes, a three-veined approximately 4-mm lemma hairy along its lower nerves and a tiny midvein mucro, not a long awn. Glume-to-lemma ratios differ among sources; do not identify from a rigid ratio without a measured ripe spikelet.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against T. flavus, both can have open drooping heads and bare proximal branch sections; compare shorter flexuous Texas panicle plus ~1/2-length glumes and lower-half lemma nerve hairs. Against T. albescens, separated drooping branch-end spikelets versus a narrow crowded spike are useful, but mature glume/lemma characters seal the ID. Eragrostis secundiflora can resemble rosy heads; check multi-flowered Tridens spikelet and dorsal three-nerve lemma anatomy.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare same-scale mature panicles, glumes and dorsal lemma nerve hairs
field_matrix.look_alike: Often a medium-sized perennial bunchgrass with a tight, lance-shaped upright panicle (Kew ~8–25 cm); appressed branches carry crowded green-to-white/purplish spikelets. Both existing photographs show this distinctly. Compare with purpletop's open head and Texas tridens' flexuous exposed branches. Check nearly equal glumes and restricted lemma-nerve hair distribution under hand lens; current photos are habit only.
field_matrix.avoid_false_identification: Color, bare branch segments and height overlap; never assert tiny hairs visible in whole-plant photo.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare same-scale mature panicles, glumes and dorsal lemma nerve hairs
field_matrix.look_alike: Large perennial with broadly open, many-branched, often nodding panicle (commonly 15–35 cm). Red/purple spikelets in bloom frequently mature dull tan; the two local pictures demonstrate both phases. Compared to Texas tridens, purpletop tends more expansive and larger but panicle lengths overlap; both can show exposed branch bases. Check flattened basal sheaths, short hair-fringe ligule, mature lemma nerve hairs, and possibly sticky panicle branches rather than treating stickiness or color as a mandatory ID.

For real ID compare the mature glumes about half lemma length and lemma-nerve hairs below midlength; avoid relying on rosy color, panicle droop or bark/soil habitat alone.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: TEXAS TRIDENS: identify a perennial tuft with an open, flexuous often nodding 8–15 cm panicle, its lower lateral branch sections relatively bare and 6–10-flowered spikelets clustered toward branch ends. Purpletop can ALSO have bare branches; confirm glumes, three-veined lemma and short hairy ligule from a ripe dissected specimen.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form: Tufted perennial; older Texas treatment describes approximately 30–60 cm flowering culms, often slightly bent at the base, and narrow basal leaves. Collar/throat may be hairy. True ligule is a ring of VERY SHORT HAIRS; no calibrated species-specific mm length established from existing photographs.

reproductive_measurements.panicle: Historical Texas treatment approximately 3–6 inches (about 7.6–15.2 cm), loose, with distant flexible branches and groups of 3–12 spikelets toward branch tips.
reproductive_measurements.spikelets: Approximately 6–11 mm long and 6–10-flowered in Silveus's Texas grass treatment; count on ripe intact spikelet, not a detached floret.
reproductive_measurements.glumes: Two thin one-veined outer glumes, lower approximately 2–3 mm, upper slightly longer; shorter than the adjacent ~4 mm lemma in the historical treatment.
reproductive_measurements.fertile_lemma: Approximately 4 mm, three-veined, shallowly two-toothed; lower portions of all three veins hairy, midvein projects as a very short mucro, lateral veins usually do not reach the margins.
reproductive_measurements.palea: Nearly lemma-length, narrowed above, two-keeled in historical Texas treatment.
reproductive_measurements.awns: No long needlelike awns; a minute excurrent midvein/mucro is NOT a long awn.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.source_reconciliation: A photographed field account describes the glumes as roughly as long as a lemma, while Silveus's measured treatment gives 2–3 mm lower glume versus ~4 mm lemma. Record the measured historical range but DO NOT use a rigid glume:lemma ratio as a sole ID until local specimens are dissected and compared. Existing older canonical phrase 'roughly half as long as the lemmas' is a provisional simplification, not a pixel-verified ratio.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Tridens flavus often taller with much larger open drooping panicle, but color and exposed lower branch segments overlap. Tridens albescens has narrower crowded appressed branches and nearly equal glumes; Eragrostis secundiflora has different spikelet/lemma anatomy. Measure several ripe florets and compare true ligule rather than pink color.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Source-vouchered local rooted perennial and one complete open flowering panicle with centimeter scale, showing actual branch insertion and spikelet clusters.
Intact 6–11 mm mature spikelet with a 1-mm ruler, showing 6–10 florets and two persistent glumes after floret shedding.
Dissect and separately measure both glumes (~2–3 mm lower in Silveus) and an approximately 4-mm three-veined fertile lemma at 10–20×; resolve historical ratio discrepancy.
Back of same-plant lemma at 20–40× showing basal hairs on THREE veins, two apical teeth and tiny midvein mucro; only add arrows to resolved pixels.
True inner blade/sheath ligule HAIR RING with 0.5-mm scale; matched T. flavus and T. albescens spikelets photographed at same magnification.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tridens texanus — first recognize the head, then verify spikelet parts
steps: See the first SOURCE-LABELLED PHOTO: use gross branches and spikelets as starting clues, not independent expert taxon confirmation.
Compare second photo to learn variable maturation/color/branch posture.
At 10–20× on a real ripe specimen, remove a spikelet and measure the paired outer GLUMES against a fertile LEMMA.
Examine hairs on the 3 raised LEMMA NERVES; this is a principal separation, but no current photo proves it.
Check 0.2–0.5 mm hairy ligule/collar and basal sheath on the SAME rooted plant; leave tentative Tridens sp. if reproductive anatomy absent.

CC0 photos are now physically archived: photographer-labelled spikelet and hairy ligule-region views are visible in local gallery panels 2–3, but neither supplies a verified millimeter ruler or independently resolved individual lemma-nerve hairs.

The archived CC0 flowering-habitat photo (panel 4) shows a source-labelled northern Uvalde County plant, not an independently traced same-plant root-to-panicle voucher; keep the Hays county range hold.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Species-level Tridens confidence requires panicle architecture PLUS mature spikelet/glume/lemma anatomy; do not identify from pigmentation alone.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Bare panicle branch bases are not unique to Texas tridens. Source-labelled photos do not establish unreviewed county nativity.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short flexuous panicle; hanging spikelet groups
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow a living culm to its full, usually 8–15 cm, loose to moderately open panicle. Long bare proximal portions of fine arching branches lead to groups of spikelets. Existing panels 0–1 illustrate gross architecture; the bare branch section ALSO occurs in purpletop, so it is not decisive alone. Archived CC0 panel 4 now adds a genuine Uvalde County flowering-habitat view; the roots and flowering stems are not traceable as one plant.
field_id_short_tiles.status: VISIBLE GROSS STRUCTURE; WHOLE ROOTED PLANT GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK GROWTH AND COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial tuft; ligule a very short hair ring
field_id_short_tiles.details: Trace flowering stems to a perennial crown; older Texas descriptions give roughly 30–60 cm culms, often bent near base. Open the true inner blade/sheath junction: a very short ligule of hairs, separate from longer throat/collar hairs. Panel 3 is source-labelled as a collar view but has no calibrated ligule measurement; do not infer a precise mm cutoff. Panel 3 is physically archived from Gaiacoyote's source-labelled original; a pale hair fringe is visible but its free margin and length are not calibrated. Panel 4 is habitat, NOT a collar macro.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL ARCHIVED COLLAR-REGION PHOTO; MEASURED LIGULE AND ROOTED CROWN GAPS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT ONE MATURE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.details: Historical Silveus Texas Grasses treatment gives mature spikelets about 6–11 mm with approximately 6–10 florets. Panel 2 is a source-labelled dissection view, but its scale and floret count are not independently certified here. Keep one entire spikelet attached to a 1-mm ruler before separating bracts. Panel 2 now exists as a physical GitHub JPEG, not merely a remote reference; the glumes and floret count still require calibrated pixel-level verification.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOCAL SOURCE-LABELLED SPIKELET PHOTO; CALIBRATED MACRO NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES ARE NOT LEMMAS
field_id_short_tiles.details: Historical Silveus treatment: thin 1-veined glumes, lower about 2–3 mm and upper slightly longer; fertile lemma about 4 mm with three veins, hairs below the middle along its nerves, and two tiny apical teeth. Another field account describes glumes approximately lemma-length; this source disagreement prevents a rigid glume:lemma ratio test. The projecting midvein is a minute mucro, not a long awn.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · COMPARE THE LOCAL TRIDENS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Purpletop overlaps; white tridens is tighter
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 7–8 are purpletop (T. flavus), which usually has a larger, wider, drooping panicle but can also have empty lower branch segments and pink spikelets. Panels 5–6 are white tridens (T. albescens), generally with narrower crowded appressed heads. Do not confuse these comparison photographs with Texas tridens. Mature glumes and hairy lemma nerves are needed when panicles overlap.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS LOOK-ALIKE LESSON; MATCHED MACROS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PROVE THE ANATOMY BEFORE 100%
field_id_short_tiles.short: Measure collar, glumes, lemma and tiny mucro
field_id_short_tiles.details: To close the card, obtain a voucher-confirmed same-plant series from rooted tuft through flowering head, then one 6–11 mm spikelet and separated glumes/three-veined hairy lemma under 10–40× with millimeter scale. Add arrows only when actual hair lines, glume boundaries and mucro are resolved. Preserve existing photo rights and any Hays nativity holds.
